column1: # research/claimcheck-block-scope-round2's tools/claim_check.py (round 2: any heading level closes scope; a
# block closes at its own table/paragraph boundary; a close marker works anywhere on a line). Scanned:
# research/findings/*.md added since 2026-09-01 on main (git log --since=2026-09-01 --diff-filter=A
# --name-only), 351 candidates, 348 present on disk at scan time, run from inside the
# research/claimcheck-block-scope-round2 worktree so cited artifact paths resolve. The `line=value` columns are
# round 2's own reported "unsupported" hits and are UNCHANGED from the original 2026-09-25 scan (reproducible,
# CORRECTED 2026-09-25, round-3 review (research/claimcheck-block-scope-r3). The original header here asserted
# "all 58 newly-failing docs fail via genuinely-exposed unsupported numbers, zero via MISSING-artifact or
# LOW_COVERAGE alone" -- worded as if "round 2's checker flags this value as unsupported" were PROOF the flag
# is a genuine error. That begs the question under review: round 2 had its own corpus-verified false-positive
# bug (a marker's block protected only ONE first-encountered unit -- a list got no persistent kind the way a
# table did, so "marker + intro sentence + list" or a list's own 2nd+ bullet fell outside protection). The
# MECHANICAL part of the old claim was correct and is RE-VERIFIED below, not just re-asserted: of these 58 rows,
# 57 fail via `unsupported` alone and 1 via `unsupported`+`low_coverage` together -- ZERO via missing-artifact
# ALONE or low-coverage ALONE (re-run against round 2's own `_scan()`, 2026-09-25 round-3). What was NOT
# verified, and should not have been implied, is that a value the checker calls "unsupported" is thereby a
# REAL error -- 3 rows were spot-checked line-by-line and are exactly the false-positive shape (correctly
# `<!--derived-->`-marked, legitimately-derived per-seed re-quotes, not previously-hidden real errors): line 19
# of 2026-09-21-load-bearing-fraction-6seed-adequate-0.85-robust-core-20.md (in this scan's window, below) plus
# two docs from BEFORE the 2026-09-01 window this scan used (2026-08-01-W5-affective-theory-of-mind-6seed-GO.md,
# RE-DERIVED, not asserted: each row below now carries a `round3=<STATUS>` field, computed by running the SAME
# doc through research/claimcheck-block-scope-r3's fixed `tools/claim_check.py` (a list gets a persistent
# block_kind exactly like a table's; fenced code blocks are transparent to heading/scope logic -- neither bug
# round 2 had). RESOLVED means the fix's own re-scan found NO unsupported/missing/low_coverage for that doc --
# i.e. this row's flags are now confirmed to have been exactly the list-scope false-positive shape. Of 58: 21
# RESOLVED, 37 STILL_FLAGGED (with the round-3 `_scan()`'s own reason: unsupported / missing / low_coverage,
# same three-way split re-derived, not assumed). STILL_FLAGGED is NOT itself a verification that a row is a
# genuine error -- it only means the round-3 fence/list fixes do not explain it; one was spot-checked
# <!--derived--> marker anywhere near it in the source doc -- an unmarked claim, a document-authoring issue,
# not a scope bug) and the rest are unverified individually; each would need its own line-by-line check before
# being called a real error, exactly the discipline this correction restores.
